claims.text: The proposed HEA variant has low stacking-fault energy.
The proposed HEA variant is derived from CoCrFeMnNi through controlled minor additions.
The HEA variant and baseline stainless steel can be closely matched in grain size, precipitate distribution, and other microstructural features.
The baseline austenitic stainless steel has a stacking-fault-energy profile similar to that of the HEA variant.
At high strain rates, low stacking-fault energy in the HEA variant facilitates deformation twinning alongside dislocation glide.
Deformation twinning supplies an additional mode of plastic deformation.
Formation of deformation twins increases strain hardening.
Twinning-enhanced strain hardening increases dynamic strength and improves the strength–ductility trade-off.
Under identical dynamic-loading conditions, the HEA variant will develop a significantly higher deformation-twin density than the matched stainless-steel baseline.
Under identical dynamic-loading conditions, the HEA variant will exhibit greater strain hardening than the matched stainless-steel baseline.
Under identical dynamic-loading conditions, the HEA variant will exhibit greater dynamic strength than the matched stainless-steel baseline.
The increase in twin density will correspond to the increase in strain hardening and dynamic strength.
The proposed mechanism applies to low-stacking-fault-energy systems under high-strain-rate loading at room and cryogenic temperatures.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to high-stacking-fault-energy or phase-unstable systems.
